correctness.rationale: If f is k-complete on a semigroup with zero, the preimage of zero under f also maps to zero under the product map and hence is zero. Any nonzero y with y^k=0 would produce another preimage of zero, at f^{-1}(y). Each zero sandwich entry in the Rees matrix produces such an element for every k>=2. Conversely, for nonzero p=p_{lambda,i}, the fixed-(i,lambda) multiplication is g*p*h in group coordinates, with identity p^{-1} and inverse p^{-1}g^{-1}p^{-1}; zero is its own one-element group. No subgroup can contain a nonzero element whose square is the absorbing zero. In a completely regular semigroup the maximal subgroups partition the elements, and in each, inversion is an involution with x(x^{-1})^2=x^{-1}. This checks the finite equivalence, necessity for all k>=2, and the infinite completely regular sufficiency, without using enumeration. As a check on the stated k=1 contrast, in B_n one may set f(i,j)=(j,i+j mod n), fixing zero; the product map sends (i,j) to (i,i+j mod n), so both maps are bijective.
residual_risks: The stored finite checks are corroboration only and the uploaded checker was not executed. No sufficiency for odd k>2 or classification of arbitrary infinite semigroups was inferred.

As a new finding, however, this specialization closes no additional classification gap or supplies a new invariant: the stronger classification gives the same obstruction and specializes to the identical construction, while the coordinate translations are immediate Rees multiplication. No separately substantial new remainder was established.
residual_risks: This judgment is about the value of the frozen finding as a distinct result, not its pedagogical utility.
